places.now: Pentonville area of Islington, north of King's Cross; the original street is probably gone or renamed
places.reason: Penton Place was a real Pentonville street, but I only know the district, so this point is approximate.

places.now: Plymouth, Devon, a city and naval port
places.reason: The text names the well-known port city, not the Plymouth Leat the gazetteer matched.

places.now: Rochester High Street, where the shops are modern
places.reason: Pumblechook is a fictional corn chandler on the High Street of Dickens's Rochester-based town, so this is only a High Street guess.

places.now: The Parade, Leamington Spa; the Regent Hotel building there is no longer a working hotel
places.reason: The Royal Hotel is probably a fictionalised version of the Regent Hotel on the Parade, which Dickens knew, so the location is a guess.

places.now: Not a point; the former empire is now Russia and neighbouring states
places.reason: It is a joking name for a whole empire, and the gazetteer's match to a statue in Kaliningrad Oblast is wrong.

places.now: The Saône river, e.g. at Chalon-sur-Saône
places.reason: The Saône is a real river in eastern France, but the exact spot in the novel is uncertain, so the point is at Chalon-sur-Saône; the Besançon match is a Doubs village and wrong.

places.now: Cursitor Street area, off Chancery Lane; the pub is fictional and nothing survives
places.reason: The Sol's Arms is a fictional pub in Cook's Court, which is generally identified with Cursitor Street near Chancery Lane.

places.now: Fictional; no real site
places.reason: Sowerberry's shop is in Mudfog, an unnamed fictional town in Oliver Twist.

places.now: St Andrew Holborn church, beside Holborn Circus; rebuilt after wartime bombing
places.reason: This is a well-documented Wren church on Holborn Viaduct, with its churchyard once a burial ground.

places.now: Gone; the Victoria Embankment and Temple Pier now stand there
places.reason: Temple Stairs were river steps at the foot of the Temple, lost when the Embankment was built, so the exact spot is approximate.

places.now: Saffron Hill area, Holborn; the old rookery has been cleared and rebuilt
places.reason: A pub of this name stood in Saffron Hill, though Dickens's Cripples is partly fictional, so the point is an approximation.

places.now: Brentford area; probably no such inn today
places.reason: The gazetteer entry places the inn at Brentford, but the name is likely a fictionalised riverside inn, so this is an educated guess.

places.now: Taunton Deane, the valley around Taunton in Somerset
places.reason: The Vale of Taunton Deane is a real valley around Taunton, but it covers a wide area, so the point is the vale's centre.

places.now: The Victorian Banbury Cross at Horse Fair/Banbury town centre
places.reason: Dickens alludes to the nursery rhyme; the old cross was destroyed in the 1600s and the present cross dates from 1859, so the spot is approximate.

places.now: Marshland on the Thames near Cliffe, Kent; no visible battery
places.reason: The Battery is fictional, set on the Thames-side marshes of the Hoo peninsula near the Cooling/Cliffe area, so this is a guess.

places.now: Rochester, near Restoration House; Satis House is a fictional composite
places.reason: The brewery belongs to fictional Satis House, partly modelled on Restoration House in Rochester, so this is only a plausible location.

places.now: Not a place; the empire no longer exists
places.reason: It is a political entity, and the gazetteer's match to a Nuremberg address is wrong.

places.now: Western Cape and Eastern Cape provinces, South Africa; Cape Town is the old capital
places.reason: The Cape Colony was a large region, so Cape Town is only a representative point, and the gazetteer's seal colony is wrong.

places.now: The Historic Dockyard Chatham, now a museum
places.reason: This is the famous Royal Navy dockyard on the Medway, where Dickens lived as a child.

places.now: Fictional; no known real site
places.reason: The Commercials is a hotel in the unnamed Rochester-like town of Great Expectations and no real building is clearly identified.

places.now: Marshland of the Hoo peninsula near Cooling, Kent
places.reason: The marsh country of Great Expectations is tied to Cooling and the Thames estuary, but the novel's marshes are not one exact spot.

places.now: Twickenham riverside area; the house is fictional
places.reason: Meagles's Cottage is fictional, set by the Thames near Twickenham, so this is only an area guess.

places.now: Demolished; the site is around Wood Street, off Cheapside
places.reason: The Cross Keys was a real coaching inn in Wood Street, long since demolished, so the exact spot is uncertain.

places.now: Not a place; it is a figure of speech
places.reason: Dickens uses it metaphorically for the Veneerings' house, and the Australian match is wrong.

places.now: Great Yarmouth town centre; the Dolphin is fictional and no inn of that name is known
places.reason: The Dolphin is a fictional inn in Yarmouth in David Copperfield, so the point is only the town centre.
